section.title: Key-Value Data — dict, Map, Object & Document
section.subtitle: How Python dicts, Java Maps, JS objects and MongoDB documents store and retrieve data by key.

topics.title: Creating Key-Value Data
topics.learn: Declaring an empty or pre-filled store.

python.definition: dict literals use {key: value}. dict() or dict.fromkeys() build them programmatically; keys must be hashable (immutable).

java.definition: Maps come as interfaces: HashMap (fast, unordered), LinkedHashMap (insertion order), TreeMap (sorted). Created via constructors or Map.of() factories.

js.definition: Object literals use {key: value}. Keys are strings (or symbols); values can be anything including functions and nested objects.

mongo.definition: A document is a BSON object — like a JSON object with typed values (_id is auto-added). Documents group into collections (like tables).

topics.title: Reading & Writing Values
topics.learn: Getting and setting values by key.

python.definition: Access via d[key]; assignment d[key] = v adds or overwrites. .get(key, default) avoids KeyError for missing keys.
python.code:
user = {'name': 'Alice', 'age': 30}
print(user['name'])        # Alice
user['city'] = 'Paris'     # add key
user['age'] = 31           # update

print(user.get('zip', 'N/A'))  # safe default

java.definition: map.get(key) returns value or null; map.put(key, value) inserts/updates; putIfAbsent and computeIfAbsent offer atomic variants.

js.definition: obj.key or obj['key'] reads; assignment writes. The in operator and optional chaining (?.) handle missing keys safely.
js.code:
const user = { name: 'Alice', age: 30 };
console.log(user.name);       // Alice
user.city = 'Paris';          // add
user.age = 31;                // update

console.log('zip' in user);   // false
console.log(user.address?.city); // undefined-safe

mongo.definition: Read with find()/findOne() using query operators; update with updateOne/updateMany using $set, $inc, $push.

python.definition: Values can be any object — lists, dicts, sets nest freely. No schema enforced; mixed types per key are allowed.

java.definition: Generics allow nested types: Map<String, List<String>>, Map<String, Map<String,Integer>>. Values are strongly typed per declaration.

js.definition: Objects nest infinitely — objects inside objects, arrays of objects, functions as values. JSON.stringify serialises the whole tree.

mongo.definition: Documents nest sub-documents and arrays natively — a user doc can embed address, orders[] with line items, etc. 16MB doc limit applies.

python.definition: .items() yields (key, value) tuples; .keys()/.values() iterate just one side. Dict comprehensions build new dicts in one line.

java.definition: entrySet() gives Set<Map.Entry<K,V>> for key+value loops; forEach with BiConsumer is the modern idiom.

js.definition: for...in loops keys, Object.entries() gives [key, value] pairs, Object.keys()/values() give arrays. for...of works on entries().

mongo.definition: find() returns a cursor you iterate document-by-document; aggregation pipeline ($project, $group) reshapes results server-side.

topics.title: JSON Serialization
topics.learn: Converting key-value data to/from JSON text.

python.definition: json.dumps() turns dicts/lists into JSON strings; json.loads() parses back. dict ↔ JSON maps cleanly since JSON objects are dict-like.
python.code:
import json
user = {'name': 'Alice', 'age': 30, 'tags': ['dev']}

text = json.dumps(user)      # str
back = json.loads(text)      # dict

# file round-trip
with open('user.json', 'w') as f:
    json.dump(user, f, indent=2)

java.definition: Jackson (or Gson) serialises POJOs ↔ JSON via annotations. Maps serialise natively too — keys become JSON property names.

js.definition: JSON is native: JSON.stringify(obj) → string, JSON.parse(str) → object. undefined/functions are dropped; Dates need toJSON or revivers.

mongo.definition: MongoDB stores BSON natively — documents are already JSON-like, so no serialisation needed for storage. Export via mongoexport to JSON/CSV.

topics.title: Choosing the Right One
topics.learn: When each key-value structure fits best.

python.definition: dict is Python's default map — fast lookups, used everywhere (kwargs, JSON, namespaces). Ordered by insertion since 3.7.
python.code:
# Best for: config, JSON data, memoization,
# counting (collections.Counter), grouping

from collections import Counter
words = ['a', 'b', 'a']
print(Counter(words))  # Counter({'a': 2, 'b': 1})

java.definition: HashMap for speed, LinkedHashMap for order, TreeMap for sorting, ConcurrentHashMap for threads. Immutable Map.of() for constants.

js.definition: Plain objects for small fixed-shape data; Map for dynamic keys, iteration order guarantees, and non-string keys. Set for unique values.

mongo.definition: Documents fit schemaless/varied data, nested structures, and horizontal scale. Use when data is document-shaped (users, products, logs) not table-shaped.
